gallery.title: File:Eyüp Sultan Mosque - Fountain.jpg
gallery.description: The Eyüp Sultan Mosque is situated in the Eyüp district of Istanbul, outside the city walls near the Golden Horn. The present building dates from the beginning of the 19th century. The mosque complex includes a mausoleum marking the spot where Eyüp (Job) al-Ansari, the standard-bearer and friend of the Islamic prophet Muhammad, is said to have been buried.

gallery.title: File:Istanbul Eyüp Türbesi Shrine in 2015 5051.jpg
gallery.description: The room one visits is complicated. Guidebook Strolling through Istanbul mentions this as a vestibule, then states: “… the türbe of Eyüp, an octagonal building three sides of which project into the vestibule”. So what I named “Shrine” are those three sides. The pictures show its outside, or the part one can look into in more or less detail.

gallery.title: File:Istanbul Eyüp turbesi Relics in 2015 5045.jpg
gallery.description: In a glass-covered recess there are several relics. A notice in 2015 explained (Google translated) “Our Prophet Master[‘s] Blessed Footprint; Sakal-I Sheriff (hair of his beard), Hacer-I Natik (Stone Talking To Our Master), Our Prophet Master[‘s  The] Leaves Of The Tree He Placed, Green Colored Tile Of Ravza-I Mutahhara“.
